question: Assume today is 2026-09-05. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of new passenger cars (Pkw) registered in Germany in September 2026, as it will be first reported in the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt's (KBA) monthly press release on vehicle registrations.

target.what: Number of new passenger cars (Pkw) newly registered in Germany during September 2026 (domestic Pkw-Neuzulassungen), as first reported by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt in its monthly vehicle-registration press release.
target.cadence: monthly press release/FZ 10, normally first published after month-end
target.caveats: The target period is future relative to the 2026-09-05 cutoff: only the first few days of September have elapsed, so this is a forecast, not a nowcast. KBA 'Neuzulassungen' are domestic first registrations of new Pkw, not production, wholesale sales, retail sales, exports, or deliveries; they exclud

candidates.hypothesis: September 2026 Pkw registrations should be anchored on the KBA monthly series: target ≈ recent monthly run-rate × September seasonal ratio × year-over-year momentum, with calendar adjustment. Prior September values and the latest published months constrain both level and trend.
candidates.data_to_find: KBA monthly Pkw-Neuzulassungen for January 2023 through August 2026, published on or before 2026-09-05, especially September 2023, September 2024, September 2025, August 2026, and any revisions or preliminary-vs-final notes. Minimum evidence: monthly totals plus dates of publication; if revised tables are unavailable, use the first-reported KBA press-release figures and annual/calendar tables as substitute.

candidates.hypothesis: September’s share of annual or monthly registrations and the number of effective registration days are structural inputs: target ≈ expected annual total × September seasonal share, or trailing 12-month average × September index, adjusted for weekdays and holidays. Stable historical seasonal ratios can constrain the forecast when current monthly data are sparse.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly German Pkw registrations for 2010-2025 with September values and September shares of annual totals; September/August ratios; number of weekdays and public holidays by German state in September 2026; KBA working-day adjustment methodology if published. Minimum evidence: a multi-year September seasonal pattern and September 2026 calendar; if KBA-adjusted working-day series is unavailable, count weekdays and state holidays manually.

candidates.hypothesis: New-car orders and dealer/fleet sentiment lead registrations by roughly weeks to a few months. If order intake, dealer expectations, and consumer climate before September 2026 are stronger or weaker than the recent norm, September registrations should move in the same direction after allowing for delivery lags.
candidates.data_to_find: Leading indicators published on or before 2026-09-05: ifo automotive business climate for July/August 2026, ZDK dealer surveys, GfK/Nuremberg consumer climate, KBA brand-level August 2026 registrations, fleet order intake, and dealer order backlogs. Minimum evidence: at least one order/sentiment indicator with a historical relationship to KBA monthly registrations; if ZDK is unavailable, use ifo and consumer climate as substitutes.

candidates.hypothesis: Scheduled policy changes can pull registrations into or out of September 2026: purchase incentives, company-car taxation, CO2 fleet rules, registration deadlines, or tax changes effective around 2026-09-30/2026-10-01 or 2027 can create timing effects. If no binding change occurs, this route implies a neutral adjustment.
candidates.data_to_find: German and EU passenger-car policies known by 2026-09-05 that affect registration timing: BAFA/EV subsidy status, company-car benefit-in-kind rules, Kfz-Steuer changes, EU CO2 fleet targets, any registration deadline at end-September 2026, and announced model/regulatory changes. Minimum evidence: effective dates and whether they incentivize earlier or later registration; if no scheduled change is found, document that no shock adjustment is justified.

candidates.hypothesis: Registrations are constrained by available new-car supply: target ≈ available domestic supply plus imports minus exports and inventory change, multiplied by sell-through. Plant shutdowns, import bottlenecks, model launches, or inventory build can shift September registrations away from the demand-only baseline.
candidates.data_to_find: German passenger-car production and exports (VDA/Statistisches Bundesamt), import registrations, dealer inventory days, plant shutdown/restart schedules, semiconductor or parts shortages, and model-launch timing, all published on or before 2026-09-05 for July/August 2026. Minimum evidence: a recent production/import/inventory signal that can constrain supply; if production data are unavailable, use KBA import-brand registrations and dealer inventory reports as substitutes.

candidates.hypothesis: Published forecasts for the German 2026 passenger-car market can constrain September: target ≈ annual forecast × September seasonal share, or a published September monthly forecast if one exists. Forecasts are intentions/expectations, not observations, so they should be used as a cross-check.
candidates.data_to_find: Forecasts published on or before 2026-09-05 for German 2026 Pkw registrations or light-vehicle sales from VDA, ifo, S&P Global Mobility, ACEA, Reuters/Bloomberg consensus, and any prediction-market contracts. Minimum evidence: an annual 2026 German market forecast plus seasonal share, or a monthly September forecast; if only European forecasts exist, combine with Germany’s historical share as a substitute with caution.

candidates.perspective: vehicle registration office and calendar observer
candidates.hypothesis: Pkw registrations occur through administrative registration offices and are sensitive to effective business days: target ≈ daily registration run-rate × effective registration days. September 2026 weekday count, state public holidays, office closures, and e-registration capacity can shift the monthly total.
candidates.data_to_find: September 2026 calendar for Germany by state, public holidays, school-holiday timing, known registration-office closures or capacity constraints, KBA registration-office lists, and any early-September 2026 daily/weekly registration counts available by 2026-09-05. Minimum evidence: effective registration-day count and calendar anomalies; if daily counts are unavailable, use the calendar and KBA working-day methodology.

candidates.hypothesis: Online new-car search and dealer lead activity can signal near-term purchase intent: higher-than-seasonal search/lead volume in August and early September 2026 should, if the historical lead relationship holds, point to higher September registrations. Because the attention-to-registration bridge is indirect, this is mainly a directional cross-check.
candidates.data_to_find: Google Trends for Germany queries such as 'Neuwagen', 'Auto kaufen', and 'Pkw Neuzulassungen' through 2026-09-05; mobile.de or AutoScout24 traffic/listing views and dealer lead volumes if available; historical correlation of such attention measures with KBA monthly registrations. Minimum evidence: a historical correlation or a clear seasonal benchmark; if unavailable, use only as qualitative context.

The best computed estimate is [[estimate]] [[unit]] for new passenger car (Pkw) registrations in Germany during September 2026, as first reported by the KBA. The supplied interval is [[p10]] to [[p90]] [[unit]] ([[interval_level]]; [[interval_basis]]).

Two methods were combined with weights [[m1_weight]] and [[m2_weight]]. The adjusted route ([[m1_estimate]]) scales the observed September 2025 total [[p56_value]] by assumption [[a1_value]] (range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]]), reflecting August 2026 momentum, BEV growth, private-share gains, improved ifo expectations, and the retroactive EV subsidy. The naive benchmark ([[m2_estimate]]) reuses [[p56_value]] with no 2026 momentum, anchored partly on [[p14_value]].

Only the prior-year totals are observed; the 2026 year-over-year factor is an assumption, and the naive route is a transfer. The main risk is that September 2026 year-over-year diverges from August momentum. Better evidence would be early-September 2026 registration data or order intake, which is unavailable at the cutoff.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
